title: Catch a regression with an independent judge
summary: Run the generated agent, score its responses, then prove that a changed answer fails the same evaluation cases.
prerequisites: Complete the repository installation: Node.js 22+, npm ci, then npm run build.
Use Bash or another POSIX shell on macOS/Linux; use WSL on Windows. Run commands from the cloned repository root.
The checked-in verify.mjs helper only reads the tutorial outputs and checks the expected facts. All agent actions still use the visible Instrilo commands.
outcome: Two saved reports and a comparison that identifies both regressed cases.

verification.scope: The real CLI, generated native TypeScript agent, deterministic assertions, judge protocol, and comparison all execute against the included local fixture.
limitations: The fixture is not an LLM: it returns fixed responses and a string-based judge score.
Dataset provenance remains synthetic; these are workflow tests, not evidence of production model quality.

steps.title: Create the agent and start the demonstration service
steps.body: The fixture binds only to an ephemeral localhost port, needs no API key, and automatically stops after ten minutes. The EXIT trap also stops it if a later step fails.
steps.code:
set -eu
INSTRILO_PROJECT=.studio/tutorials/evaluate-and-compare
node dist/cli.js init evaluate-and-compare --directory .studio/tutorials
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/fixture.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.log" 2>&1 &
INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID=$!
trap 'kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/control.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" ready
steps.expected: The readiness check prints zero runtime/judge/tool requests.

steps.title: Assign runtime and judge separately
steps.body: The connection files are written by the fixture using its chosen local port. Distinct model IDs exercise independent role selection. The two checked-in cases are synthetic on purpose.
steps.code:
node dist/cli.js connections add runtime-fixture "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture/runtime.json"
node dist/cli.js connections add judge-fixture "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture/judge.json"
node dist/cli.js connections use runtime runtime-fixture "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js connections use judge judge-fixture "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js cases import "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file examples/quickstarts/delivery/cases.jsonl --replace
node dist/cli.js build "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js prepare "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: Generated code and its runtime dependencies are ready. prepare downloads normal npm dependencies; it does not call a model.

steps.title: Save the passing baseline
steps.body: The actual generated agent calls the local runtime connection; Instrilo sends each result to the separate judge connection.
steps.code:
node dist/cli.js eval "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --split development --output "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/reports/baseline.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/verify.mjs baseline "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: Both cases pass deterministic checks and receive a fixture judge score of 1.

steps.title: Introduce and detect a regression
steps.body: Only the local fixture answer changes. The dataset, configuration, guidance, and judge stay unchanged. Evaluation exit 1 is expected here and is explicitly checked; its failed report is still saved.
steps.code:
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/control.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" bad
INSTRILO_EVAL_EXIT=0
node dist/cli.js eval "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --split development --output "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/reports/regression.json" || INSTRILO_EVAL_EXIT=$?
test "$INSTRILO_EVAL_EXIT" -eq 1
node dist/cli.js compare "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/reports/baseline.json" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/reports/regression.json" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/comparison.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/verify.mjs comparison "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/control.mjs "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture" counts > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture-counts.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/verify.mjs eval-counts "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID"
wait "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" || true
trap - EXIT
steps.expected: The comparison lists billing-escalation and ticket-reference as regressions with passRateDelta:-1. Counters show four runtime and four judge calls. The fixture then stops.

next.label: Review outputs and inspect the release gate

troubleshooting: Use a fresh tutorial project name if init says the directory already exists. The commands create files and reports that deliberately refuse overwriting existing results.
Read the printed error and instrilo help --all before retrying. A failed assertion means the observed result differs from this guide.
An existing report path is intentionally rejected. Use a fresh project or choose a new report filename rather than overwriting evidence.
If the fixture times out, start a fresh walkthrough; its random endpoint is part of the project configuration and evidence fingerprint.
cleanup: The tutorial creates only its named project under .studio/tutorials. Keep reports if useful; remove that project directory when you no longer need it.
